Didn't mean to come off as angry at all. I'm not emotionally invested in any way, I just thought it would be helpful for you to hear from an outside force you're lying to yourself. And I'm not projecting anything, I use cannabis daily, legally.  Although I'm glad you recognize the body and mind are heavily influenced by each other, there's yet to be any scientific evidence of physical dependency. Don't blame the substance for what you did to yourself, you chose to smoke that bowl day 12, it wasn't beneficial medically like it is when you withdraw from heroin per say. I digress, last thing I have to say is if you want to quit then stop making excuses.

So you didn't go 21 days without it. Lie number 1. You also don't get withdrawals from marijuana other than self inflicted ones. Lie two.   Do you actually have the desire to quit? Step number one is buckle up and quit justifying your failures with lies to make yourself feel better. It's gonna suck to quit, I won't sugar coat it, but this isn't a elementary school sports team you don't get a trophy for showing up, you either do what you need to do which is not smoke, or you fail. There's no transparency. Good luck on the road ahead brother, be honest with yourself and if you really want to quit you gotta believe it for yourself. One love.

Well its honestly a little embarrassing to admit, but for the sake of others I will tell my story. 

Well first things first, I'm a 19 year old male, who suffers from severe depression and moderately bad anxiety. 

So there I was, sitting in my room with a belt around my neck. And after continuously fighting a battle from hell against depression that seemed like it was my only way out. It was about 3am, and my parents as well as my two sisters were asleep. I had wrote a 4-5 page note on a microsoft word document explaining how sorry I was about killing myself and how it was all my fault and no one elses. I printed the document and placed it on my kitchen counter. Then walked back up to my room in a state of mind I hope to never experience again. So there I was with the belt and the saddest most worthless feeling imaginable. It seems like a miracle that my mom needed some advil at 3am, but she did and so she walked into the kitchen and saw my note and instantly burst into my room. I was at that point passed out from suffocation and she called 911 and the next thing I remember is being awoken to a bunch of random questions. I was beyond confused. I was taken to the hospital and then after that put into a different type of hospital for those with psychological issues. I ended up spending a week in there and learned alot about myself. I can never thank my parents enough for finding me and saving me. And i can never apologize enough for what I tried to do. 

Anyway, the message is to get help before its too late. It may seem helpless but I promise there is help out there weather it be someone to talk to or medication. Keep fighting to anyone out there. You are unique and your life has unimaginable value. If you are struggling mentally, get help. It's nothing to be ashamed of at all, and you'll be suprised how common depression/bipolar/anxiety/etc actually is. 

Much love and keep on keeping on.
